svg.title: Blackbody radiation curves
svg.desc: EM radiation intensity versus wavelength for a blackbody at 6000 K (white hot), 4000 K and 3000 K (red hot), drawn to scale from Planck’s law. The 6000 K curve peaks near 480 nm, inside the visible range; cooler bodies radiate far less, and their peaks move to longer wavelengths: about 720 nm at 4000 K and 970 nm, in the infrared, at 3000 K. Ultraviolet lies to the left of the visible band and infrared to the right.
